cards.canonical_statement: If real sequences u and v converge to a and b, respectively, their pointwise sum converges to a + b.
cards.proof_strategy: Apply continuity of real sum to the pair of converging sequences.
sketch_steps: Fix both real sequences and their limits.
Combine their convergence into convergence of the pair.
Real sum is continuous on the pair space.
Apply this continuous operation to the converging pair.

cards.canonical_statement: If u→a and v→b with b≠0, the sequence u(n)/v(n) converges to a/b.
cards.proof_strategy: Use continuity of division at a pair whose denominator limit is nonzero.
sketch_steps: Retain both convergence assumptions.
Check the limit b of the denominator is nonzero.
Division is continuous at (a,b).
Apply continuity to obtain the quotient limit.

cards.canonical_statement: If u(n) converges to a, then |u(n)| converges to |a|.
cards.proof_strategy: Apply continuity of real absolute value to the convergent sequence.
sketch_steps: Fix u and its limit a.
The absolute-value function is continuous everywhere.
Compose the sequence with absolute value.
The resulting limit is the absolute value of a.

cards.canonical_statement: A real sequence cannot converge to two different real limits.
cards.proof_strategy: Apply uniqueness of limits in the Hausdorff real topology.
sketch_steps: Fix one sequence u.
Assume convergence to both a and b.
The natural atTop filter is nontrivial and ℝ is Hausdorff.
Uniqueness of limits gives a=b.

Pass to the limit and retain the non-strict inequality.
